verdict_basis: Every A1-A6 claim reproduced independently, and every recorded comparison was recomputed exactly with separate code. Ledger accounting is sound. Nothing protected changed. The findings are three low-severity runbook/test hazards and four informational notes. None blocks the paid run. F1 and F2 would require editing RUNBOOK.md and re-freezing.

environment.network_isolation: Every test, controller plan, verifier and recomputation run executed under `unshare -rn` (no network namespace).

findings.title: Step 10 final observation fails when no pod id was ever bound
findings.evidence: POD is set only in step 5 (RUNBOOK.md:100), once SSH is bound. F4 create_rejected (:222), F4 with no pod listed, and early F9/T paths route to 'steps 9 and 10' with POD unset. Running `observe_account.py --pod-id $POD --out X` with POD empty (offline, no network) exits 2 with 'argument --pod-id: expected one argument', so no final account observation is recorded.
findings.fix: Replace `--pod-id $POD` with `${POD:+--pod-id $POD}` at RUNBOOK.md:189, or give no-pod branches an explicit command without --pod-id. This changes RUNBOOK.md, which FREEZE.json binds, so the freeze must be rebuilt.

findings.title: Create is gated on user approval by step order only
findings.evidence: Invariant 7 requires recorded approval before create. Step 2 (RUNBOOK.md:58-62) writes $RUN/USER_APPROVAL.json, but the step-4 command does not test for it. The unchanged controller's create (bundle/controller/lease.py:827-902) takes no approval input. Nothing mechanical stops an out-of-order or pasted create.
findings.fix: Prefix the create line with `test -s $RUN/USER_APPROVAL.json &&` (pipelines bind tighter than &&, so tee is unaffected). Also requires re-freezing. Otherwise root must observe the order manually.

findings.title: Re-running any acceptance test overwrites frozen evidence in place
findings.evidence: save_evidence always writes into D/evidence with write_text. Re-running A2-A6, whether by a reviewer or as post-run re-verification, replaces files that FREEZE.json binds; A2 embeds a fresh lease name and deadlines. `build.py verify` then fails at build.py:163. To re-execute without modifying D, I redirected `common.EVIDENCE` in-process (scratch run_test.py). build.py verify still passed after all my runs and after the concurrent writer.
findings.fix: No bundle change is needed for the run. Anyone re-running the tests must redirect EVIDENCE as above, never run in place. If tests are edited for other reasons, make the write exclusive (open 'x') or take an output directory.

findings.title: Ten deviations are listed, not eight
findings.evidence: The deviations section has items 1-10. All ten match the code: download_model.py is run at bootstrap.py:61 and is byte-identical; test_lifecycle.py is identical to precision_v1; the [160] composite is recomputed first and last; the fallback exit step is 3 (validate_outputs.py:47, which also covers zero matches); inputs are fresh contiguous copies and only target rows are saved; M2 has no physical hooks; the GPU name equals attempt05's recorded 'NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090'; the worker diff against precision_v1 is limited to the documented removals plus the phase rename 'native_logit_measurements' and dropping bank_records from provenance; A4 has no fallback; the lease root is diagnostic_native_logit_v1.
findings.fix: None required. Refer to ten deviations in later documents.

findings.title: torch_equal is not bit-exactness
findings.evidence: Adversarial case signed_zero_consistent_record: a row differing from the reference only by -0.0 versus +0.0 records torch_equal=true with differing_elements=1, and the verifier correctly accepts it. No such divergence occurred on CPU (bitwise_differs_but_torch_equal = []).
findings.fix: Post-run analysis of objective 3 ('reproduces native final logits bit-exactly') must require differing_elements == 0. torch_equal alone is not sufficient. No code change.

findings.title: Verifier does not bind token_ids to the development items
findings.evidence: Adversarial case token_ids_substituted_same_length: token IDs replaced by same-length IDs, with a consistently regenerated record, are accepted. The binding relies on the pinned worker source (worker.py:135-139, 171) and on the exact M2-versus-M1 logits comparisons.
findings.fix: In the post-run CPU reanalysis, retokenize the three historical items through the unchanged old-item path and require token_ids to match (S = 20, 15, 13). No bundle change.

findings.title: Any file written into the round root during the run trips F11
findings.evidence: inventory.py compare allows only cloud_leases/diagnostic_native_logit_v1/. My own before/after compare flagged the concurrently written reviews/diagnostic_native_logit_v1_review.{json,md} as added_unexpected (status changed, exit 1). A RUN_LOG.md entry or review file written between steps 0 and 10 would therefore raise a false F11 'invariant violation'. Controller writes outside the lease root are limited to opening the existing cloud_leases/.lease_creation.lock in append mode, which leaves its hash unchanged.
findings.fix: Take the step-0 inventory only after all A7 reports are written, and defer RUN_LOG.md/review writes until after step 10. Alternatively, record intended additions and pass them as extra --allow-added prefixes.

3_independent_recomputation.method: Separate script; validate_outputs is never imported. Bits come from raw bytes; values come from a hand bf16 decoder (checked equal to torch's exact float64 cast) and numpy float64. torch.equal semantics = numeric equality; bitwise count = any differing byte per element; math.fsum means; stable descending top-k via numpy. A first pass had a decoder bug (wrong exponent bit field), caught by the decoder self-check and fixed; every figure here is from the corrected run.
3_independent_recomputation.evidence: Record names and order identical to my contract-derived list (255 = 3 + 3 x 84). All 255 records equal my recomputation field for field. exit_steps equal; every token's exit step is 3 on CPU. Every shape, dtype and finiteness value matches the contract: M1 [3,192,2048] and [3,49152] f32; runs [4,1,S,2048], [1,S,2048] and [1,S,49152] bf16 plus virtual191 [2048] f32; recomputations [2,2048] / [2,49152] bf16. The 23 M1-M4 coverage checks all pass. norm_input[3,0,-1] == virtual191.
3_independent_recomputation.m3_construction: Rebuilt all shaped inputs independently and re-ran RMSNorm and F.linear from snapshot weights (model.norm.weight, lm_head.weight present, tie_word_embeddings false, eps 1e-6) on CPU. All 23 recomputation families x 2 repeats x 3 items reproduce the saved rows bit-for-bit, confirming the target-row placement and the cycled fill semantics.
3_independent_recomputation.layout: Captured lm_head_input, lm_head_output and logits are contiguous with storage offset 0, so deviation 5's fresh copies match the native layout. On CPU, logits share storage with lm_head_output.
3_independent_recomputation.gpu_payload_estimate: Re-serializing with separate logits storage (as GPU .cpu() copies produce) gives 46,360,421 bytes for the three large payloads, plus ~16 KB for provenance and run_spec: under the 50 MB contract limit, with ~3.6 MB margin.
